He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|11|in|m|2}} and {{convert|235|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions. ==Early career and high school career== Petrušev was born in [[Belgrade]], [[Republic of Serbia (1992–2006)|Serbia]], [[Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|FR Yugoslavia]]. He started to play basketball for youth teams of Serbian powerhouses [[KK Crvena zvezda (youth)|Crvena zvezda]] and [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].{{cite web |title=SALE MOŽE DA BIRA Podmladiti "orlove"? Ima tu ZLATA VREDNOG talenata |url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/sale-moze-da-bira-podmladiti-orlove-ima-tu-zlata-vrednog-talenata/n45jj1l |website=sport.blic.rs |access-date=7 August 2018}} In 2014, Petrušev signed for youth team of Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia|Laboral Kutxa]]. Petrušev began playing high school basketball in 2016 with [[Avon Old Farms]] in [[Avon, Connecticut]].{{cite web|title=A look into Filip Petrušev|url=https://agent49.net/intro-filip-petrusev/|website=agent49.net|access-date=20 January 2018}} In July 2017, he had transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] where he played senior season.{{cite web|title=FIBA u18 A: Filip Petrusev recruitment set to pick up|url=https://www.scout.com/Article/FIBA-u18-A-2018-Serbian-post-Filip-Petrusev-recruitment-set-to-pick-up-105820429|website=scout.com|access-date=20 January 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Petrušev was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], according to major recruiting services. He originally committed to Hartford on October 24, 2016 and later decommitted on July 26, 2017. On October 22, 2017, he announced his commitment to Gonzaga. On November 8, 2017, Petrušev signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] with the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]].{{cite web|title=Highlights of Gonzaga bound forward Filip Petrusev|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Highlights-of-Gonzaga-bound-forward-Filip-Petrusev-113937139|website=247sports.com|access-date=20 January 2018}}{{cite web|title=Serbian big |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/no-gonzaga-looks-to-extend-streak-vs-no-byu/article_5b3438a0-90b9-5814-95ca-3bc5d8f2beb0.html |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] agent |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29104748/gonzaga-filip-petrusev-enter-nba-draft-not-hire-agent |access-date=April 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 27, 2020}} ==Professional career== === Mega Soccerbet (2020–present) === On July 20, 2020, Petrušev signed his first professional contract with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Soccerbet]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]]. "There's a lot of uncertainty with the NCAA season," he said. "Here I should be able to showcase some skills I wasn't able to at Gonzaga and improve my draft stock."{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Gonzaga center Filip Petrusev to sign pro deal in Serbia |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29503437/gonzaga-center-filip-petrusev-sign-pro-deal-serbia |access-date=July 20, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 20, 2020}} He was named the [[ABA League Player of the Month Award|ABA League October MVP]].{{cite web |title=MVP OF OCTOBER: Filip Petrušev (Mega Soccerbet) |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/44007/mvp-of-october-filip-petrusev-(mega-soccerbet)/ |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=4 November 2020}} On November 8, Petrušev withdrew from the 2020 NBA draft.{{cite web |title=Filip Petrusev withdraws from 2020 Draft |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1125493/filip-petrusev-withdraws-from-2020-draft/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=November 8, 2020 |date=November 8, 2020}} He won the [[ABA League MVP]], [[ABA League Top Prospect]], and [[ABA League Top Scorer]] awards for the [[2020–21 ABA League First Division|2020–21 season]].{{cite web |title=Filip Petrušev osvojio triplu krunu u ABA ligi |url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/filip-petrusev-osvojio-triplu-krunu-u-aba-ligi/385720 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=29 April 2021}} On 3 May 2021, Petrušev declared for the [[2021 NBA draft|2021 NBA Draft]].{{Cite web|title=JOŠ JEDAN SRBIN KRENUO KA NBA - I TO NAJTALENTOVANIJI: Filip je DOMINIRAO u ABA, sada je vreme za glavnu nagradu!|url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Kosarka/a1466778/filip-petrusev-se-prijavio-za-draft-2021-mega-aba-liga-kosarkasi-srbije.html|access-date=2021-05-04|website=Mondo Portal|language=sr}} ==National team career== Petrušev was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-16 basketball team|Serbian U-16 national team]] that participated at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]{{cite web|title=Serbia 12 - Filip Petrusev|url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/116212/sid/11538/tid/96799/tid2//_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men/index.html|website=archive.fiba.com|access-date=20 January 2018}} and [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]].{{cite web|title=Serbia 12 - Filip Petrusev|url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/116212/pid2//sid/12295/tid/96799/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U16_European_Championship_Division_A/index.html|website=archive.fiba.com|access-date=20 January 2018}} Petrušev was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-18 basketball team|Serbian national under-18 basketball team]]s that won the gold medals at the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2017 Championship]] and the [[2018 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. Over seven tournament games in 2017, he averaged 5.3 points and 3.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Player Profile at the 2017 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2017/Filip-Petrusev|website=FIBA.com|access-date=20 January 2018}}{{cite web|title=Gonzaga basketball signs Filip Petrusev of Serbia|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/11/09/gonzaga-basketball-signs-filip-petrusev-of-serbia/107498450/|website=usatoday.com|access-date=20 January 2018}} In 2018, he averaged 21.0 points, 8.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game over seven tournament games.{{cite web |title=Filip PETRUSEV 2018 FIBA Profile |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2018/player/Filip-Petrusev |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=6 August 2018}} Petrušev had 29 points, 8 rebounds and 3 assists in the Final. At the tournament's end, he finished third in scoring and rebounds and got selected to the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web |title=Serbia big man Pecarski named MVP, tops All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2018/news/serbia-big-man-pecarski-named-mvp-tops-all-star-five |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=6 August 2018}} Petrušev was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-19 basketball team|Serbian under-19 team]] that finished 7th at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 19.3 points, 10.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.6 steals and 2.0 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Average Statistics of Serbia at the 2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball
